question: A chord AB and a diameter CD of a circle (with center O) intersect each other at a point P(outside the circle) and BP is equal to the radius of the circle. If ∠APC = 35°, then what is the measure of ∠AOC?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a circle, when a secant passing through the center and another secant intersecting the circle meet at an external point P.

If the external segment of the intersecting secant is exactly equal to the radius of the circle (BP = r).

Then, the central angle subtended by the larger arc is always exactly three times the external angle at P.

Direct formula for this specific case: ∠AOC = 3 × ∠APC

⇒ ∠AOC = 3 × 35° = 105°

**∴ The correct answer is 105°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Center of the circle is O, and its radius is r. So, OA = OB = OC = OD = r.

Secant PAB and secant PCD (passing through the center) intersect at external point P.

BP = radius of the circle = r, and ∠APC = 35°.

 35° r r r O P C D A B ∠AOC = 3 × ∠P = 105° 

**Calculations:**

⇒ In ΔOBP, OB = r (radius of the circle) and BP = r (given).

⇒ Since OB = BP, ΔOBP is an isosceles triangle.

⇒ Angles opposite to equal sides are equal, so ∠BOP = ∠BPO = 35°.

⇒ Using the exterior angle theorem in ΔOBP, the exterior angle at B is ∠OBA.

⇒ ∠OBA = ∠BOP + ∠BPO = 35° + 35° = 70°.

⇒ In ΔOAB, sides OA and OB are both radii, so OA = OB = r.

⇒ Since ΔOAB is an isosceles triangle, ∠OAB = ∠OBA = 70°.

⇒ Now, looking at ΔOAP, the exterior angle at O is ∠AOC.

⇒ By the exterior angle theorem, ∠AOC = ∠OAP + ∠APO.

⇒ ∠AOC = 70° + 35° = 105°.

**∴ The correct answer is 105°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Secant Angle Theorem

When two secants intersect outside a circle, the measure of the angle formed is half the difference of the measures of the intercepted arcs: ∠P = (m(arc AC) − m(arc BD)) ÷ 2.

Exterior Angle Theorem

The exterior angle of a triangle is exactly equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles. Formula: ∠Ext = ∠Int₁ + ∠Int₂

Isosceles Triangle Property

If two sides of a triangle are equal, then the angles opposite to those sides are also strictly equal in measure.
